To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aggregate vascular risk factors are associated with postmortem cerebral vascular changes and that the presence of cerebral vascular changes is associated with a lower Braak and Brak stage.
aggregate vascular risk is associated with CVC in AD and that CVC is associated with a less severe AD pathology.
the presence of multiple, rather than any individual, vascular risk factors was related to CVC and that the presence of CVD was associated with less AD pathology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between cerebrovascular disease and dementia, and how these two conditions may interact.
the relationship of vascular risk factors and the development of Alzheimer's disease (dementia).
the role of vascular risk factors and their impact on the development of Alzheimer's disease (and other dementias).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a strong association between vascular risk factors and dementia.
the evidence for a causal relationship of vascular risk factors and Alzheimer's disease is not yet established.
there is no evidence of any effect of statins on cognitive performance, dementia, or AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of multiple risk factors for vascular disease is associated with the presence of Cerebrovascular Changes (CVC) and the severity of CVC is associated with lower AD severity.
the aggregate effects of vascular risk are associated with cerebrovascular pathology, and this may be associated with a delay in the progression of Alzheimer's disease pathology.
the presence of multiple risk factors for cerebrovascular disease is associated with the presence of cerebrovascular pathology in autopsy-confirmed AD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vascular risk is a major factor in the etiology of AD, and that vascular risk factors may be modifiable.
aggregate vascular risk factors are more predictive of cerebrovascular pathology than individual vascular risk factors.
aggregate risk factors are more important for cerebrovascular changes than single risk factors.
